# pi-runtime/vendor (populated by scripts)

This folder is generated by `npm run pi-runtime:fetch` (or `:fetch:win` on
Windows). It is intentionally checked out empty so the repo stays small —
the bundled Node + pi-coding-agent tree is ~80 MB.

After running the fetch scripts you'll see something like:

```
vendor/
├── node-darwin-arm64/        macOS Apple-silicon Node 22 binary
├── node-darwin-x64/          macOS Intel
├── node-linux-x64/           Linux for the dev shell
├── node-win-x64/             Windows
└── pi/                       npm install of pi-coding-agent + extensions
    ├── package.json
    └── node_modules/
```

The Tauri bundler glob in `tauri.conf.json` (`bundle.resources`) walks
this folder at build time and copies it into the app bundle.

If you're starting fresh:

```bash
cd desktop
npm run pi-runtime:fetch        # Mac / Linux
npm run pi-runtime:fetch:win    # Windows
```

If you're seeing "glob pattern …pi-runtime/vendor/** path not found", the
Cargo build script is complaining that this folder is empty. Either run
the fetch script above, or temporarily remove the `pi-runtime/vendor/**`
entry from `bundle.resources` in `tauri.conf.json`.
